RagShortTexts: Situated across critical crossroads, Vandals maintained fortified border networks anchored against rivers, mountain passes, and dense forests.
Under intense pressure from migrating populations and rival expansion, the borders faced acute strain from regional upheavals.
Frontier governors exercised broad emergency prerogatives, maintaining patrol outposts and garrison bastions to shield agrarian heartlands.

Variants.Content: The territorial perimeter of Vandals spanned treacherous terrain encompassing river crossings, mountain defiles, and primeval woodlands. Shielding the arterial supply corridors leading toward Silesia & Upper Danube, the regime garrisoned fortified outposts and watchtowers tasked with round-the-clock reconnaissance. In 374 AD, strategic volatility reached a fever pitch, aggravated by border clashes and cross-frontier raiding. Provincial commanders operated under persistent resource deficits, forced to contain covert banditry while preparing against full-scale royal invasions, knowing that any fatal rupture along the forward limes would unleash catastrophic devastation upon undefended inland communities.

On the palisade above the Silesian plain, the watch counts campfires in the valley below. Enemy horsemen have raided the outer farms three times this month, and every embrasure now holds a loaded ballista. A sentry who dozes at his post will be the first body the raiders find at dawn, and his comrades will bury him without ceremony.

At the border fort, the Vandal warden unseals a dispatch from the chancery and finds the subsidy cut once more. Without silver to hire auxiliary companies, he must trade land rights with neighboring petty lords to keep the passes guarded. Each season the raiders probe closer, so every sealed report he sends now ends with a plea for funds before the snows block the roads.
